h: A Few Pointers Before You Tee Off
p: Puttshack comes from the same brothers who founded Topgolf, and it's built around what the company calls Trackaball technology. Each ball is tracked as you play, so the scoring updates automatically and the holes can respond to your shots with lights, sounds and surprises. It turns crazy golf into something that feels more like a game show.

To get the most out of your round, watch how the first hole works and take a peek at the scoring screen so you understand what's going on. Some holes reward careful aim, others are all about luck, so don't take it too seriously. Mix up who putts first to keep it fair, and try to pace your group so you're not holding up the players behind.

Bringing the family? Puttshack venues often have restrictions on children at certain times, especially later in the day, so check the age policy before booking. Daytime and early evening tend to be the best times for younger players.

Watford has plenty more to explore. Watford Museum, in a handsome old building on the High Street, tells the story of the town, from its brewing and printing heritage to its football club. Speaking of which, Vicarage Road is home to Watford FC, and match days give the town a real buzz. For a gentle walk, the Grand Union Canal towpath is lovely, with narrowboats and green views.
Book ahead for evenings and weekends, and arrive a little before your slot.
